# Navigating Interconnection Queue Complexities

Dorrit Naskhollow: Welcome back to The Xandra Dispatch. Today, we’re diving into a thorny topic in grid-scale battery storage—interconnection queues. Joining me is Niamh Vaskstead, lead engineer at Voltara Energy Solutions. Niamh, thanks for being here.

Niamh Vaskstead: Glad to be here, Dorrit.

Dorrit: So, interconnection queues have been a real bottleneck for large battery projects. What’s the core issue causing these delays?

Niamh: It’s a perfect storm, really. Utilities are swamped with applications, many from solar and wind folks plus battery storage players. The queue in the Midline Regional Grid alone jumped from 300 projects in 2020 to nearly 900 by late 2023. That sheer volume overwhelms the technical studies needed—like impact assessments and system upgrades.

Dorrit: Wow, tripling in just three years? Any examples from your recent work?

Niamh: Definitely. We had a 100 MW battery project slated for East Crest, originally expecting connection within 18 months. But with queue delays and required transformer upgrades, it stretched to nearly 42 months—more than double. That kind of timeline can kill project economics.

Dorrit: That’s brutal. How are companies like Voltara navigating this?

Niamh: We’re leaning heavily into early engagement with utilities and proposing modular interconnection points. Instead of a single large connection, we break the project into stages, each with its own smaller queue spot. It helps manage risk and sometimes fast-tracks partial dispatch.

Dorrit: Clever. Any policy moves on the horizon?

Niamh: Some regulators are piloting “fast-track” processes for proven tech and smaller upgrades, plus pushing utilities to increase staffing for queue management. But it’s early days.

Dorrit: Niamh, thanks for shedding light on this. Listeners, we’ll link to Voltara’s whitepaper on queue strategies in the episode notes. Stay tuned for more on improving battery dispatch software next week.
